narrative.overview:
Mark Gordon's homepage puts him where he belongs: in front of leaders who need practical help with culture, trust, and relationships. The visitor should feel they have found a seasoned speaker and facilitator — not a course catalog or marriage blog.

Visual identity stays committed cobalt with cool neutrals. What changes is hierarchy: a text-first hero with typographic authority, one dominant CTA (Book Mark to Speak), differentiated offering layouts, and fewer stronger sections.

The system rejects WordPress-era patterns (video-split hero, identical product cards, course grids on homepage) while preserving brand recognition.
keyCharacteristics: Text-first hero with sentence-case h1 at display scale
Book Mark to Speak as the single dominant CTA
Differentiated layouts for keynotes, workshops, and coaching
7–8 homepage sections maximum — no course grids
Cobalt band rhythm without nested identical cards

rules.name: The Hero Exception Rule
rules.body: Only the homepage h1 uses hero typography (sentence case, clamp scale). Section h2s stay uppercase display.

rules.name: The One CTA Rule
rules.body: Book Mark to Speak is the primary label at hero, challenge, and final close. Contextual secondaries (Explore Coaching, Explore Workshops) appear only on their offering panels.

rules.name: The Committed Blue Rule
rules.body: Cobalt Conviction may occupy 30–60% of visible surface on marketing pages. Never gradient text or decorative stripes.

rules.name: The Band Rhythm Rule
rules.body: Section depth alternates through background color (Clean Surface / Cool Band / Cobalt Conviction), not nested cards.

rules.name: The No-Courses-on-Home Rule
rules.body: Individual course cards and tabbed mini-courses do not appear on the homepage. Courses live under Resources.

dos: Do lead with a text hero and Book Mark to Speak above the fold on mobile
Do differentiate keynote, workshop, and coaching offering layouts
Do use short testimonial excerpts with leadership framing
Do repeat the primary CTA at hero, challenge, and final close
Do keep paragraphs to 2–4 lines on mobile
donts: Don't put course grids or audience-path forks in the hero
Don't use identical dark-header ProductCard rows for all offerings
Don't repeat Book Discovery Call four times with the same label
Don't use video in the homepage hero
Don't feature Leadership Accelerator until its page exists
Don't use buzzword copy: empower, transform, flourish, unlock
